Mia Chen: quick heads-up — ran a cross-quant bakeoff (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8) on the new gptx-small variant and saw a reproducible accuracy drop for AWQ/INT8. suspect per-channel activation outliers in a handful of layers. want to propose a small toolchain + runbook for per-channel thresholding and an onboarding check.
Sam Patel: sg. can you paste the minimal repro log and which infra you ran it on?
Mia Chen: ran on dedicated-bakeoff-2 (p4d). minimal log:```
layer 23 activation max by channel: [0.12, 0.09, 10234.5, 0.10, ...]
channels with max>1e3: [2, 67, 128]
AWQ int8 accuracy delta: -1.9% vs fp16 baseline
GPTQ int8 delta: -0.2%
```
Mia Chen: note: these spikes only show up in some eval sets (long-tail prompts), not in random 1k tokens sample.
Andrew Li: are you thinking absolute clamp thresholds or percentile-based? we used 99.999th percentile heuristic before which caught some but not these.
Mia Chen: thinking adaptive per-channel: clamp = median + k * MAD (median absolute deviation) with fallback to per-layer percentile if MAD==0. keeps scale aware. k tunable per model.
Eva Gomez: there9s a small prototype in my fork: https://git.internal/redwood/tools/chan-thresholding (WIP). CLI looks like:```
python tools/chan_thresh.py --model gptx-small --quant awq --eval /data/evals/longtail.json --out results.json --k 10
```
quant-ci-bot: CI run finished for branch eva/chan-thresh — summary: AWQ int8 pre-clamp: -1.9% ; post-clamp (adaptive k=10): -0.3% ; GPTQ int8 unchanged. full:```
metric,pre,post
ll_mean,-2.15,-0.42
acc_top1,0.814,0.806
```
Praveen Rao: nice. proposal: add a model-onboarding gate that flags any layer where >0.5% of evaluation tokens exceed the per-channel clamp threshold. this should surface fragile models early.
Sam Patel: from deployment POV — do we enable adaptive clamp by default on hosted inference? or expose as a model-profile opt-in?
Mia Chen: prefer opt-in via model profile key `clamp: adaptive` and do a canary rollout (10% traffic) for hosted. Dedicated/Private customers can enable per their SLA. documented in runbook.
Andrew Li: add unit tests + micro-bench. worried about perf: does clamp add KV writes or other overhead?
Eva Gomez: benchmarked locally — clamp path adds a tiny extra conditional but no KV writes; observed ~1.2% median latency increase at 1-token contexts, within our SLO envelope. will add microbench in PR.
Mia Chen: runbook draft steps I9ll add to the PR: 1) reproduce with `tools/chan_thresh.py`, 2) run `tools/plot_channel_spikes.py` to generate histograms, 3) run full eval pre/post clamp, 4) add test to `model-catalog/tests` with fixture, 5) create rollout config `clamp:adaptive` with canary and fallback to fp16/gptq variant.
Mia Chen: example histogram command:```
python tools/plot_channel_spikes.py --in results.json --layer 23 --out /tmp/l23.png
```
Praveen Rao: also add a lint gate in onboarding that auto-creates a ticket for models with >5 flagged layers. i9ll take ownership of the model-catalog side changes.
Mia Chen: TODO list: - reproduce and attach results to PR; - add unit + microbench; - add onboarding lint flag; - add canary rollout policy. will ping @Praveen Rao when PR is up.
Sam Patel: :thumbsup: please tag me for the canary rollout review.
quant-ci-bot: scheduled nightly perf sweep for branch eva/chan-thresh (ETA 6h).
